release: AuraBoot CRM product gate (RG-1 through RG-4 verified subset)

run.target: All AuraBoot CRM product pages and Cordys-parity action surfaces
run.runtime: static denominator; qualifying pass rows point to real-stack evidence sources

goals.note: 26/26 semantic actions and five workbenches have real-stack browser evidence.
QDP release and order commitment have true-stack and browser evidence.
Clean-room automation passes; independent non-developer human sign-off is still pending.
This committed manifest is freshness-gated and mutation-falsifiable.
Selected forecast submissions are compared with live owner facts and drilled down to exact opportunity drivers.

The governed external Customer Request intake command and its read-only source-evidence summary have true-stack and browser evidence; actual Email/Portal connectors and Excel UX remain outside this slice.

Three real-stack journeys cover member operations, manager batch work, administrator governance, recycle policy, ownership evidence, import/mobile behavior and negative boundaries without development-data migration.
A self-seeded real-stack journey verifies contact primary/enable-disable invariants and the Web follow-up plan/record lifecycle without development-data migration.

A self-seeded browser journey converts a qualified lead and proves that direct and relation-anchored follow-up activities, comments and deduplicated customer history remain visible across the resulting account, contact and opportunity graph.

A self-seeded two-person browser journey proves owner isolation, read-only and editable collaboration, expiry, renewal, revoke, notification, collaborative-account filtering and cross-tenant fail-closed behavior.

A self-seeded browser journey creates one governed customer relationship fact from account detail, proves outgoing and incoming projections, edit persistence, self/missing/duplicate rollback, uniqueness and confirmed deletion.

untested.reason: A developer-authored automation run cannot prove that a person who did not participate in development completed the browser journey.
